message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"10.1","text":"On the third day in Tripolis, then, Peter rose from sleep rather early and entered the garden, where there was a large reservoir into which abundant water flowed continuously. There he bathed; then, after praying in this way, he sat down. Realizing that we were sitting around him and gazing intently at him as though we wanted to hear something, he said:","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὀρθριαίτερον","chosen":"rather early","rationale":"The comparative adverb indicates an earlier-than-usual or notably early hour; “earlier in the morning” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"ὑδροχοεῖον μέγα","chosen":"a large reservoir","rationale":"The noun denotes a receptacle or reservoir for water; “large water basin” is a viable alternative."},{"source_quote":"εἶθ’ οὕτως εὐξάμενος","chosen":"then, after praying in this way","rationale":"οὕτως most naturally qualifies the praying as “thus/in this way,” though it may function more loosely as a sequential “thereupon.”"},{"source_quote":"ἡμᾶς δὲ περικαθεζομένους","chosen":"we were sitting around him","rationale":"The participle portrays the group seated around Peter; the object “him” is supplied from the immediate context."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"10.2","text":"“There seems to me to be a great difference between the ignorant and those who have gone astray. For the ignorant person seems to me to resemble a man who chose not to set out for a flourishing city because he did not know the good things there, whereas the person who has gone astray resembles one who learned of the city’s good things but, while setting out along the road, turned aside from the path and therefore wanders. In the same way, then, there seems to me to be a great difference between those who worship idols and those who wander in the worship of God. For those who worship idols are ignorant of eternal life (and for that reason they do not even desire it, since they cannot love what they do not know); but those who have chosen to worship the one God and have learned that eternal life is given to the good, if they either believe or do anything contrary to what God approves, resemble those who have left the city of punishment but to come to the flourishing city ... and who, while on the road, have strayed from the straight way.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῶν ἀγνοούντων πρὸς τοὺς πεπλανημένους","chosen":"between the ignorant and those who have gone astray","rationale":"The contrast is between lack of knowledge and deviation after acquiring knowledge; “those who have been misled” is also grammatically possible for the perfect passive form."},{"source_quote":"ἐπ’ εὐθηνουμένην πόλιν","chosen":"for a flourishing city","rationale":"The participle describes a city prospering or thriving; “prosperous city” is an alternative."},{"source_quote":"τρίβον παραλλάξαντι","chosen":"turned aside from the path","rationale":"The phrase depicts deviation from or missing the traveled track; “passed by the path” is more formally possible but less suitable to the ensuing wandering."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς ἐν θεοσεβείᾳ ἀλωμένους","chosen":"those who wander in the worship of God","rationale":"θεοσέβεια can denote worship of God, reverence for God, or piety; “worship of God” best preserves the contrast with idol worship."},{"source_quote":"τὰ δοκοῦντα τῷ θεῷ","chosen":"what God approves","rationale":"The expression denotes what seems right or acceptable to God; “what seems right to God” is a more formally transparent alternative."},{"source_quote":"ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ τῆς εὐθείας πλανηθεῖσιν","chosen":"who, while on the road, have strayed from the straight way","rationale":"The genitive τῆς εὐθείας is taken with πλανηθεῖσιν as what they strayed from, while ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ supplies the setting. An attachment yielding “on the road of the straight way” is possible but less idiomatic."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"εἰς τὴν εὐθηνουμένην ... καὶ","issue":"The selected image-checked edition prints exactly three dots here, marking a lacuna that disrupts the construction after “to come to the flourishing city.” The unavailable content has not been restored, and the three printed dots are retained in the translation.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"10.3","text":"While he was discussing these things with us, one of our people came in—the man appointed to report such matters to him—and said, “Large crowds, my lord Peter, are standing before the doors.” When he gave permission, a large crowd came in. Peter rose, took his place on the platform used the day before, greeted them according to the custom of reverence for God, and said: “The human being, having come into being in the image and likeness of God—the God who created heaven and earth and made everything in them, as the true prophet told us—was appointed to rule and exercise dominion. I mean over the things in the air, on the earth, and in the waters. From the fact itself one can perceive that by his own intelligence he brings down the things in the air, brings up the things in the depths, and captures the things on the earth, even though they are far stronger than he is—I mean elephants, lions, and things like them.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὁ ἐπὶ τῷ ἀπαγγέλλειν αὐτῷ τὰ τοιαῦτα καθεστηκὼς","chosen":"the man appointed to report such matters to him","rationale":"καθεστηκώς indicates that this person had been assigned or established in the reporting role."},{"source_quote":"τῇ ἐχθὲς βάσει","chosen":"the platform used the day before","rationale":"βάσις may denote a base, stand, or raised platform; the context of public speaking favors “platform.”"},{"source_quote":"τῷ τῆς θεοσεβείας ἔθει προσαγορεύσας","chosen":"greeted them according to the custom of reverence for God","rationale":"προσαγορεύω denotes addressing or greeting, while θεοσέβεια may also be rendered “piety” or “worship of God.”"},{"source_quote":"κατ’ εἰκόνα καὶ καθ’ ὁμοίωσιν γεγονὼς","chosen":"having come into being in the image and likeness of God","rationale":"κατά expresses correspondence to an image and likeness; “according to the image and likeness” is a more formally literal alternative."},{"source_quote":"κατ’ ἀλκὴν αὐτοῦ πολλῷ μείζονα ὄντα","chosen":"even though they are far stronger than he is","rationale":"Literally, the animals are “much greater than he in strength”; the chosen wording gives that comparison idiomatic English without reducing its force."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"10.4","text":"“Yet when he was righteous, he was also above every suffering, since, with an immortal body, he was incapable of experiencing pain. But when he sinned (as we showed yesterday and the day before), he became a servant of sin and fell under every suffering, deprived by a just judgment of all good things. For it was not reasonable that, when the giver had been abandoned, the things given should remain with the ungrateful. Therefore, out of his surpassing compassion, so that, along with the original good things, we might also receive the eternal good things to come, he sent his prophet. The prophet commanded us to speak to you—to tell you what you must think and do. Make your choice, then; that lies within your power. What you must think, then, is this: to worship the God who made everything. If you apprehend him with your mind, you will receive from him, along with the original good things, the eternal good things to come.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πάντων παθημάτων ἀνώτατος","chosen":"above every suffering","rationale":"πάθημα here denotes suffering or affliction, as the following reference to pain indicates; “beyond all sufferings” is an alternative."},{"source_quote":"ὡς δοῦλος γεγονὼς τῆς ἁμαρτίας","chosen":"he became a servant of sin","rationale":"The wording portrays subjection and belonging to sin. “Slave of sin” makes the ownership nuance more explicit, while the stipulated default renders δοῦλος as “servant.”"},{"source_quote":"ἅμα τοῖς πρώτοις","chosen":"along with the original good things","rationale":"The substantivized adjective refers to the former or first good things of which humanity had been deprived; “the former good things” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"ἐλέσθε οὖν, ὃ ἐπὶ τῇ ὑμετέρᾳ κεῖται ἐξουσίᾳ","chosen":"Make your choice, then; that lies within your power","rationale":"The relative clause is taken as referring to the act of choosing. It could instead be construed as “choose what lies within your power.”"},{"source_quote":"τὸν πάντα πεποιηκότα σέβειν θεόν","chosen":"to worship the God who made everything","rationale":"The delayed θεόν is taken with the substantival participle. The syntax can also be represented as “to worship as God the one who made everything.”"},{"source_quote":"ὃν ἂν ἀπολάβητε τῷ νῷ, ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ἀπολήψεσθε","chosen":"If you apprehend him with your mind, you will receive from him","rationale":"The first ἀπολαμβάνω is understood as mentally grasping or apprehending because of τῷ νῷ, while the second means receiving from God. “When you take hold of him with your mind” is a viable alternative."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"10.5","text":"“You will therefore be able to persuade yourselves to do what benefits you if, as though chanting an incantation to the fearsome serpent nesting in your heart, you say, ‘You shall fear the Lord God, and you shall serve him alone.’ By every line of reasoning, then, it is beneficial to fear him alone, not as unjust, but as just. For one fears an unjust person lest one be unjustly killed, and the just one lest, after being caught in sin, one be punished. Through fear of him, then, you can be freed from many harmful fears. For if you do not fear the one Lord and Maker of all, you will be servants of all evils, to your own harm—I mean demons, sufferings, and everything capable of causing harm in any way whatever.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πεῖσαι οὖν ἑαυτοὺς πρὸς τὰ συμφέροντα","chosen":"persuade yourselves to do what benefits you","rationale":"The πρός phrase expresses movement toward beneficial things. “Bring yourselves around to what is beneficial” is a closer structural alternative but less direct in English."},{"source_quote":"τῷ ἐμφωλεύοντι ἐν τῇ ὑμετέρᾳ καρδίᾳ δεινῷ ὄφει","chosen":"the fearsome serpent nesting in your heart","rationale":"ἐμφωλεύω depicts making a lair or dwelling within, while δεινός here conveys the serpent’s fearsome or terrible character."},{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ ἐπᾴδοντες","chosen":"as though chanting an incantation","rationale":"ἐπᾴδω refers to singing or reciting a charm over or to someone or something; “casting a spell” is a possible but less source-transparent rendering."},{"source_quote":"τὸν δίκαιον","chosen":"the just one","rationale":"In context this most naturally refers to God as the just one, contrasting him with an unjust person. Grammatically, “a just person” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"πάντων τῶν κακῶν δοῦλοι","chosen":"servants of all evils","rationale":"The phrase expresses subjection to every evil. “Slaves of all evils” would foreground the ownership and bondage force of δοῦλοι."},{"source_quote":"δαιμόνων καὶ παθημάτων","chosen":"demons, sufferings","rationale":"πάθημα continues the sense of suffering or affliction found in the preceding section; “passions” is lexically possible but less consistent with the immediate discussion of harmful experiences."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ᾡδήτινι","issue":"The selected edition prints this as a single, unusually accented and undivided sequence. In context it is defensibly understood as the relative-plus-particle expression meaning “in any way whatever”; this is an orthographic or word-division issue rather than an unreadable construction.","proposed_reading":"ᾧ δή τινι","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
